faq.q: Combien Stripe facture-t-il par transaction ?
faq.a: Pour de nombreux paiements par carte en ligne aux États-Unis, le taux publié par Stripe est de 2,9 % + 0,30 $ par prélèvement réussi. Sur un paiement par carte nationale de 100 $, cela représente environ 3,20 $ (effectif de 3,2 %). Les cartes internationales, la conversion de devises, les remboursements et les petits billets peuvent augmenter le taux mixte – utilisez la calculatrice ci-dessus pour votre mix, puis téléchargez un solde CSV pour voir votre taux réel.

faq.q: Is this a Stripe fee estimator or a real calculator?
faq.a: The on-page Stripe fees calculator estimates fees from public pricing. Stripe Fee Auditor calculates your real effective Stripe fee rate from your Balance Transactions CSV, so you can compare the estimate with actual numbers.

faq.q: How do I estimate monthly Stripe fees?
faq.a: Enter your monthly card volume and average charge amount to estimate monthly fees. Use the reverse calculator when you know the net amount you want to receive and need the gross amount to charge.

faq.q: What file do I need to calculate my Stripe effective fee rate?
faq.a: You need the Stripe Balance Transactions CSV export. It includes the transaction amount, fee, net amount, currency, type, and timestamp needed for an accurate fee analysis.

faq.q: Why can my effective Stripe rate be higher than the published rate?
faq.a: International cards, currency conversion, refunds, Radar charges, disputes, and micro-transactions can all push your blended effective rate above Stripe's standard published rate.

faq.q: Quelle est la différence entre les rapports de solde et de paiement ?
faq.a: Les transactions de solde incluent les frais individuels, les remboursements et les frais. Les rapports de paiement sont des résumés regroupés de ce que Stripe a envoyé à votre banque. Utilisez les transactions de solde pour l’analyse des frais.

faq.q: Quelle quantité de données dois-je exporter ?

whyHigher.eyebrow: Auditeur d'honoraires · Formation indépendante en matière d'honoraires
whyHigher.heroTitle: Pourquoi mon taux effectif Stripe est-il plus élevé que prévu ?
whyHigher.heroDescription: Stripe annonce 2,9 % + 0,30 $. Votre taux effectif – et parfois votre paiement par rapport au volume – se situe souvent entre 3,2 et 3,8 % en raison des cartes internationales, des frais de remboursement non retournés, des devises et des petits billets. Voici les cinq facteurs déterminants – avec des chiffres réels. Fee Auditor vous aide à vérifier votre propre solde CSV ; nous ne sommes pas le support Stripe.

items.title: Cartes internationales
items.description: Lorsque la carte de votre client est émise en dehors de votre pays, Stripe ajoute des frais transfrontaliers de +1,5 %. Si 20 % de vos clients sont internationaux, cela ajoute à lui seul environ 0,3 % à votre tarif effectif.
items.example: 20% clients internationaux × 1,5% = +0,30% sur votre tarif effectif

items.title: Conversion de devises
items.description: Si vous facturez en USD mais que la banque de votre client règle en EUR ou en GBP, Stripe applique une majoration de change en plus du taux de base. Ceci est distinct des frais transfrontaliers et souvent invisible dans le tableau de bord.
items.example: La majoration des changes est intégrée au taux de change et n'est pas affichée sur une ligne distincte

items.title: Remboursements
items.description: Stripe keeps the processing fee when you issue a refund. The original transaction fee is not returned. A 5% refund rate adds meaningful cost across large volumes.
items.example: Taux de remboursement de 5 % sur 100 000 $ de revenus = 145 $ de frais non remboursables

items.title: Stripe Radar
items.description: If you use Radar for fraud protection beyond the basic included tier, there's an additional $0.02–$0.07 per transaction. This shows up as a separate line in your Balance report.

items.title: Micro-Transactions
items.description: On small charges, the fixed $0.30 component dominates. A $2.00 charge has an effective rate of 17.9% — this drags up your average significantly if you have many small payments.

faq.q: Pourquoi mon taux de frais Stripe est-il supérieur à 2,9 % ?
faq.a: Votre taux de frais Stripe effectif peut être supérieur aux 2,9 % + 0,30 $ publiés en raison des frais de carte internationale, de la conversion de devises, des frais non remboursables sur les remboursements, des frais de radar, des litiges et des petites transactions pour lesquelles les frais fixes représentent une part importante du paiement.

faq.q: Stripe renvoie-t-il les frais de traitement lorsque je rembourse un paiement ?
faq.a: No. When you issue a refund, Stripe generally does not return the original processing fee. This can increase your effective fee rate if your business has a meaningful refund rate.

faq.q: How can I calculate my real Stripe effective fee rate?
faq.a: Export your Stripe Balance Transactions CSV and divide total Stripe fees by total processed charge volume for the same period. Stripe Fee Auditor does this from your real CSV and shows the transactions driving the rate up.

sections.heading: Comment calculer le pourcentage réel
sections.formula: Pourcentage réel de Stripe = total des frais Stripe / volume total des frais traités
paragraphs: For one transaction, divide the Stripe fee by the charge amount. For your business, use the blended rate across a full period.

C’est le chiffre qui vous indique ce que Stripe a réellement prélevé sur vos revenus. Les frais d'une seule carte nationale de 100 $ peuvent sembler proches de 3,2 %, mais un mois réel peut atteindre 3,8 %, 4,2 % ou plus, selon la zone géographique du client et la taille de la transaction.

faq.q: Combien Stripe facture-t-il par transaction ?
faq.a: For many US online card payments, Stripe charges 2.9% + $0.30 per successful domestic card transaction. On $100 that is about $3.20. International cards often add about 1.5 percentage points, and currency conversion can add roughly another 1%. Your blended rate across a month is usually higher than any single published line — check it from your Balance CSV.

faq.q: Quel pourcentage Stripe prélève-t-il sur un paiement ?
faq.a: Pour de nombreux paiements par carte en ligne aux États-Unis, le taux publié par Stripe commence à 2,9 % plus 0,30 $ par prélèvement réussi. Le pourcentage effectif sur un seul frais dépend du montant des frais, car les frais fixes de 0,30 $ sont plus élevés pour les petits paiements.

faq.q: Why is my real Stripe rate higher than 2.9%?
faq.a: International cards, currency conversion, Stripe Billing fees, refunds, disputes, Radar, and small transaction sizes can all push your real blended Stripe rate above the headline percentage.

faq.q: How do I check the actual percentage Stripe took?
faq.a: Export your itemized Stripe Balance CSV, sum charge volume, sum Stripe fees, and divide fees by volume. Stripe Fee Auditor does this from your Balance CSV and separates processing rate from all-in Stripe cost. You can also start with the free Stripe fees calculator for a published-rate estimate.

sections.body: Les exportations BI peuvent inclure des dizaines d’objets. Pour un audit des frais Stripe, la partie importante est beaucoup plus petite : chaque ligne a besoin de suffisamment de données pour séparer le volume des frais des dollars des frais.

faq.q: Puis-je exporter Stripe directement vers JSON ?
faq.a: Oui, mais l'exportation JSON est normalement un workflow d'API ou de connecteur, et non un workflow Dashboard CSV. Si votre objectif est le rapprochement des frais, le CSV du solde détaillé est généralement plus rapide que la création d'un pipeline API complet.

faq.q: Puis-je utiliser les données Stripe dans Tableau ou Power BI ?
faq.a: Oui. Vous pouvez d'abord importer des exportations CSV ou synchroniser Stripe dans un entrepôt. Pour l'analyse des frais, assurez-vous que votre ensemble de données comprend des lignes de transactions de solde avec le brut, les frais, le net, la devise, la date de création et la catégorie de reporting.

faq.q: Fee Auditor est-il un connecteur d'entrepôt de données Stripe ?
faq.a: No. Fee Auditor is a Stripe fee analysis tool. Il ne synchronise pas votre compte Stripe avec PostgreSQL, Tableau, Power BI ou JSON. Il analyse un solde CSV détaillé pour calculer votre taux effectif réel et vos frais.

faq.q: Quelle exportation Stripe dois-je utiliser pour le rapprochement des frais ?
faq.a: Utilisez l’exportation détaillée des transactions Balance CSV ou Balance. Les CSV de paiement et les résumés de paiement peuvent être utiles, mais ils ne contiennent généralement pas suffisamment de détails sur les frais au niveau des transactions pour un audit fiable des frais.

faq.q: Stripe Fee Auditor remplace-t-il un logiciel de comptabilité ?

sections.heading: À propos du fondateur
paragraphs: Construit par Konstantin Starkov, fondateur indépendant de SaaS. J'ai créé Stripe Fee Auditor après avoir constaté à quelle vitesse le coût réel de Stripe peut s'éloigner du taux global de 2,9 % : un exemple d'exportation a montré un taux de traitement de carte de 3,82 % et un coût tout compris de Stripe de 4,02 %.
The product is intentionally narrow: one CSV export, one question, one report that explains whether fees are normal or worth investigating.

sections.heading: Pourquoi ça existe
paragraphs: Les 2,9 % annoncés par Stripe + 0,30 $ ne sont qu'une partie de l'histoire. Les cartes internationales, les petits frais, les remboursements, les litiges et les services complémentaires font augmenter le tarif mixte, souvent sans une vue claire du tableau de bord. Cet outil transforme vos données de solde exportées en un audit lisible : taux de traitement, coût global, tendances mensuelles, frais élevés et idées d'économies directionnelles.

sections.heading: Confidentialité et traitement des données

Raw CSV is not stored as a file. We parse it in memory, compute aggregates, and discard the upload body.

faq.answer: For a SaaS business with meaningful Stripe volume, a monthly fee audit is enough. Compare processing rate, all-in Stripe cost, refund count, international share, and high-fee charge drivers against the previous month.

faq.question: What is the most important Stripe fee metric to track?
faq.answer: Track both processing rate and all-in Stripe cost. Processing rate isolates charge fees, while all-in cost includes other Stripe fee rows such as disputes, Billing, Tax, Radar, and refund-related impact.

faq.question: What is Stripe fee leakage?
faq.answer: Stripe fee leakage is the gap between the headline payment rate you expect and the real all-in cost created by fixed fees, international cards, currency conversion, refunds, disputes, and add-on products.

faq.question: Which businesses are most exposed to Stripe fee leakage?
faq.answer: Low-ticket subscriptions, global SaaS, refund-heavy products, and B2B invoices paid by card are the most exposed profiles. High-ticket domestic B2B SaaS is usually safer.

faq.question: How do I measure fee leakage from Stripe data?

faq.question: What is Stripe's international card fee?
faq.answer: Stripe's international card fee is an extra cross-border fee charged when the card was issued outside your Stripe account country. For many US pricing scenarios, this is commonly 1.5 percentage points on top of standard card processing.

faq.question: Does card currency or card country decide the international fee?
faq.answer: The international card fee is driven by the card issuer country relative to your Stripe account country. Currency conversion is separate and can stack on top when the charge and settlement currencies differ.

faq.question: How do I find international card fees in Stripe data?
faq.answer: Export an itemized Stripe Balance CSV and look for international card indicators in charge rows, descriptions, or fee patterns. Then compare those rows against domestic card charges for the same period.

faq.question: Is Stripe ACH cheaper than credit cards?
faq.answer: For many large US B2B payments, ACH is cheaper than cards because ACH has a lower percentage fee and a cap. Cards can still be better for speed, conversion, and consumer checkout expectations.

faq.question: When should a SaaS business offer ACH?
faq.answer: ACH is most useful for large invoices, annual plans, and B2B customers who are comfortable with bank payments. It is less ideal for instant consumer purchases or high-friction checkout flows.

faq.question: What is the tradeoff between ACH and card payments?
faq.answer: ACH usually costs less but can settle slower, fail differently, and create more onboarding friction. Card payments cost more but are faster and familiar for many buyers.

faq.question: Why are Stripe fees so high on small transactions?
faq.answer: Stripe's fixed per-transaction fee is the same whether the charge is $5 or $100. On a $5 charge, a $0.30 fixed fee is already 6% before the percentage fee is added.

faq.question: What is the Stripe fee on a $5 payment?
faq.answer: Using 2.9% + $0.30 as the example rate, a $5 payment costs about $0.45 in fees: $0.145 from the percentage fee plus $0.30 fixed. That is roughly a 9% effective rate.

faq.question: How can I reduce Stripe fees for low-priced products?
faq.answer: Bundle small purchases, increase minimum charge size, move monthly micro-plans to annual billing, or batch usage-based charges into fewer invoices where the customer experience allows it.

faq.question: What is a Stripe blended rate?
faq.answer: A Stripe blended rate is total Stripe fees divided by total charge volume across a period. It blends different payment types, fixed fees, international cards, refunds, and add-on fees into one real-world percentage.

faq.question: Why is my blended rate higher than 2.9%?
faq.answer: Your blended rate can be higher than 2.9% because the fixed $0.30 fee is large on small charges, international cards add cross-border fees, currency conversion can add cost, and refunds or disputes can raise all-in fees.

faq.question: Should I use charge fees or all Stripe fees?
faq.answer: Use charge fees to measure card processing rate. Use all Stripe fees to measure all-in Stripe cost. Both are useful, but they answer different questions.

faq.question: Which Stripe CSV export should I use for fee analysis?
faq.answer: Use the Itemized Balance CSV or Balance Transactions export. Summary exports are useful for totals, but they do not contain enough transaction-level fee detail for a real fee audit.

faq.question: Where do I export a Stripe Balance CSV?
faq.answer: In Stripe Dashboard, go to Reporting or Reports, open Balance summary or Balance transactions, set the date range, choose Export, then choose Itemized and download the CSV.

faq.question: How much Stripe data should I export?
faq.answer: Export at least one full month. Three to six months is better for diagnosing fee trends, international card mix, refund leakage, and month-over-month rate changes.

faq.question: Is a Stripe payout report enough for fee reconciliation?
faq.answer: No. A payout report is useful for bank reconciliation, but it groups money movement. Use the Itemized Balance CSV or Balance Transactions export when you need transaction-level fee rows.

faq.question: Why did my Stripe effective rate jump this month?
faq.answer: The most common causes are more international cards, a lower average transaction size, refunds from a prior month, new currency conversion, Stripe add-on fees, or dispute fees.

faq.question: What month-over-month Stripe fee change is normal?
faq.answer: A movement of about 0.2 percentage points can be normal for a mixed SaaS business. A jump above 0.5 percentage points usually has a specific cause worth investigating in the Balance CSV.

faq.question: Which Stripe CSV rows should I check first?

faq.question: Why did my Stripe fees increase?
faq.answer: Stripe fees usually increase because your payment mix changed: more international cards, lower average charge size, currency conversion, disputes, refunds, or extra Stripe products such as Billing, Radar, or Tax.

faq.question: How can I tell what caused the increase?

sections.title: Short answer
sections.body: The best way to reduce Stripe fees is to match the fix to the driver: ACH for large invoices, annual billing for small recurring charges, local payment methods for international customers, and dispute/refund reduction when those rows dominate.

paragraphs: Once you're processing over $80,000/month, Stripe will discuss custom rates. Contact your account manager or reach out at stripe.com/contact/sales. Even a 0.2% reduction on $100K/month saves $200 every month.

sections.heading: 2. Increase Average Transaction Value
paragraphs: The $0.30 fixed component hurts small transactions most. Consider bundling products, offering annual plans instead of monthly, or setting a minimum order value.

sections.heading: 3. Reduce Disputes
paragraphs: Enable Stripe Radar rules to block suspicious transactions before they become disputes. Use clear billing descriptors. Each avoided dispute saves $15 + potential refund costs.

paragraphs: If you sell in multiple countries, consider enabling local payment methods via Stripe to avoid currency conversion fees (1% per transaction).

sections.heading: 5. Use ACH for High-Value B2B Payments
paragraphs: ACH bank transfers via Stripe cost 0.8% (capped at $5). For invoices over $1,000, this is 70–80% cheaper than card processing.

intro: Connecting a tool to Stripe is easy. One OAuth screen, one click, and suddenly the tool can start building charts, dashboards, alerts, and forecasts from your payment data.

That convenience is real. But so is the tradeoff. Your Stripe account contains customer records, payments, refunds, invoices, payouts, disputes, and a history of how money moves through your business. Even read access can be a bigger trust decision than it sounds.
This is why I prefer a CSV-first workflow for one-off fee audits: export the data I need, analyze that snapshot, and avoid granting a persistent connection to my live Stripe account.

sections.heading: The problem is not that OAuth is bad
paragraphs: OAuth is a legitimate way to connect software. If you need a live subscription dashboard, automated revenue recognition, or recurring operational syncs, an API connection can make sense.
The problem is that many founders treat a Stripe OAuth prompt like a harmless login button. It is not. It is a permission decision around some of the most sensitive operating data in the business.

sections.heading: What broad read access can expose
paragraphs: Stripe has more than one integration model, including Connect OAuth, Stripe Apps permissions, and API keys. The exact data depends on the model and permissions granted. But broad read access can expose categories like these:
bullets: Customer records such as names, email addresses, billing details, and tax identifiers when customer access is granted.
Charges, refunds, payment attempts, invoices, subscriptions, prices, coupons, and billing history.
Balance transactions, fee records, transfers, payouts, and cash movement through the Stripe account.
Disputes, fraud warnings, events, files, and other operational records depending on requested permissions.

sections.heading: Read-only still means copyable data
paragraphs: Read-only normally means the tool should not create refunds, update subscriptions, or change your Stripe settings. That is good. But read-only data can still be copied, processed, stored, exported, joined with other datasets, and exposed if the vendor is breached.
In other words, the important question is not only 'Can this app change my account?' It is also 'What can this app learn about my customers and business, and how long will it keep that data?'

sections.heading: Persistent access is the hidden part
paragraphs: A CSV export is a snapshot. An OAuth or API connection can be ongoing until it is revoked or otherwise limited by the integration. If you stop using a tool but forget to disconnect it, that connection may remain part of your security surface.
That does not mean every connected tool is unsafe. It means every connection deserves the same scrutiny you would give any vendor that handles customer or financial data.

sections.heading: The CSV-first alternative
paragraphs: For a fee audit, real-time access is usually unnecessary. You do not need a permanent connection to answer questions like: What is my effective fee rate? Which transactions are expensive? Are refunds leaking margin? Is my 4.5% rate normal for my mix?

Fee Auditor uses this approach. You export an itemized Stripe Balance Transactions CSV, upload it for analysis, and get a report without connecting your Stripe account. The raw CSV is not stored as a raw file; the app keeps a derived analysis result so you can reopen the link. During the promotional beta, full-report access may be free for up to 30 days; after beta, unpaid previews are shorter unless you purchase a full-report unlock — see the Privacy Policy.
